content: Scrivener's widow and landlady in Great St Helen's
Makes oak-gall ink and keeps the bread-board notch
She will not buy a second loaf to mend a finger, and she will not send a letter a day before the carrier is in.
Threepence when you sit. She will take a death in the second act. She will not have a sermon in a letter. She hopes the ground is not the point, and she does not say whose the crown is.
She boils the Monday ink, prices the loaf at a penny and a finger and a half, and does not weigh it.
She will fill the horn on a Monday and she will not take a plot with the copperas.
She will let you carry the stores, and she will not let you write the price.
